newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Turkmenistan offers cheap electricity to Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan offers cheap electricity to Pakistan.

text.p: Turkmenistan has offered to sell electricity to Pakistan at about two U.S. cents per kilowatt-hour, Pakistan's Water and Power Minister Nisar Ali Khan said on Friday.

Khan, who is also Minister for Petroleum and Natural Resources, told a news conference the offer had been made at a summit meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) in the Turkmen capital Ashgabat earlier this week.
"Two possibilties were discussed at the summit, export of electricity from Turkmenistan and export of electricity from Tajikistan," Khan said.
"And you will be amazed to know that the price they (Turkmenistan) offered us at the border for their electricity is two (U.S.) cents to a unit (kwh)," he added.
Pakistan has no border with Turkmenistan and any power deal would require transmission lines to be laid across war-torn Afghanistan.

Khan said 900 km (562 miles) of transmission lines would be needed to bring the power from Turkmenistan to the Pakistani grid and a feasibility study had already been completed. He said the final price might be even lower than $0.02 per kwh.
Khan said Pakistan already had excess electricity and had set up a committee to examine the power purchase agreements it had signed with private power producers in the past few years.

"As you know I have already set up a committee to go into power generation agreements," he said. "They have already had three meetings. The basic objective of that committee is to find ways and means by which we get private power at cheaper rates."
He said some of the electricity to be purchased from private power companies would cost eight to nine U.S. cents per kwh.
"In the next two years, it is going to multiply further, so we have to set our house in order," he said.
Khan said Tajikistan had proposed that Pakistan help it complete a big hydro-electric project in return for cheap supplies of electricity, but declined to identify the project.
Pakistan also has no border with Tajikistan, but the Central Asian republic is much closer than Turkmenistan. -- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
